systemSummary: TradeReconciler.exe is a single-project .NET Framework 4.8 console application. On each invocation it (1) drains a legacy MSMQ private queue of serialized trade messages, (2) reads a matching settlement file dropped by the custodian bank into an inbound folder, (3) matches trades to settlement records using a deterministic key + tolerance algorithm implemented in TradeReconciliationEngine.cs, and (4) writes matched.csv and exceptions.csv to an outbound folder that a downstream reporting job polls. There are no automated tests; behavior is documented only in a 2016 operations runbook and validated manually each release by Trade Operations replaying a fixed set of sample files.
components: Program.cs — entry point; wires up MSMQ listener, file readers/writers, and invokes TradeReconciliationEngine.Run().
TradeReconciliationEngine.cs — core matching logic: keys trades by (TradeId, SettlementDate), matches within a configurable amount tolerance, and classifies unmatched trades by reason.
MsmqTradeSource.cs — WCF/MSMQ adapter that deserializes binary-formatted trade messages from a private queue.
SettlementFileReader.cs — fixed-width settlement file parser tied to the custodian bank's legacy format.
ReconciliationReportWriter.cs — writes matched.csv and exceptions.csv using culture-invariant formatting.
App.config — holds the tolerance, queue name, and folder path configuration currently only editable via XML on the host.
dataFlows: Upstream trade capture system → MSMQ private queue (binary serialized TradeMessage) → MsmqTradeSource → in-memory trade list.
Custodian bank SFTP drop → local inbound folder → SettlementFileReader → in-memory settlement list.
TradeReconciliationEngine matches trade list against settlement list → MatchResult collection.
ReconciliationReportWriter → matched.csv / exceptions.csv → outbound folder polled by the downstream reporting job every 15 minutes.
constraints: The on-disk settlement file format is owned by the custodian bank and cannot change.
The output CSV schema (column order, headers, culture-invariant number formatting) is consumed by a downstream reporting job that cannot be changed in this effort.

MSMQ is Windows-only and unsupported on the target runtime; a like-for-like transport is not available on .NET 8, so the input transport must change even though the message payload/semantics must not.
The reconciliation tolerance (currently 0.01 currency units, configurable in App.config) must remain externally configurable.
No database is involved; all state is file-based and the job is expected to be idempotent-by-rerun (rerunning against the same inputs reproduces the same outputs).
knownBehaviors: Trades are matched to settlement records by (TradeId, SettlementDate); an amount difference within tolerance is still a match.
A trade with no settlement record within 3 business days of its SettlementDate is classified as exception reason 'UNSETTLED'.
A settlement record with no corresponding trade is classified as exception reason 'ORPHAN_SETTLEMENT'.
A trade matched but outside tolerance is classified as exception reason 'AMOUNT_MISMATCH' and reports the signed difference.
Duplicate TradeId+SettlementDate pairs in the input are both retained and both flagged exception reason 'DUPLICATE_TRADE_KEY' rather than silently deduplicated.
matched.csv and exceptions.csv are always written even when empty (headers only), because the downstream job expects both files to exist every run.
All monetary values are formatted with invariant culture and exactly 2 decimal places regardless of host locale.
